summary: Performed a detailed static analysis of the Pi SDK (v0.84.2) ExtensionUI contract and the existing Gizmo Pi agent service abstractions, then produced a comprehensive design document for bridging Pi extension UI calls over the WebSocket protocol. No code was changed — this is a pure research and design exploration that maps every UI method (select/confirm/input/editor/notify/setStatus/setWidget/setTitle/setEditorText), specifies new protocol messages (extension.ui.respond, extension.ui.requested, extension.ui.cancelled, extension.ui.runtime.cleared), defines a new ExtensionUIRuntime abstraction, and prescribes binding-order, reload, abort, eviction, and dispose lifecycle handling.
decisions: Bump protocolVersion from 19 to 20 to add the extension UI wire protocol.
Bind extensions with mode: 'rpc' (not 'json') so ctx.hasUI is true and extensions receive the expected rpc mode.
Use a runtimeId distinct from sessionId because reload and idle reconstruction can create a new extension runtime for the same sessionId; client must scope persistent UI state by runtimeId.

Move bindExtensions() out of createDefaultPiSession and into PiAgentService so it runs after #activate() and after session.created is emitted, avoiding a race where session_start handlers fire before the service is registered.
Use explicit null (not undefined) for clearing status/widget values so it survives JSON serialization.

Use separate message types (extension.ui.requested, extension.ui.cancelled, extension.ui.runtime.cleared) rather than reusing Unity's confirmation.requested/resolve schemas, because Pi UI has method-aware responses, timeouts, signals, runtime generations, and multiple simultaneous dialogs.
Do not serialize WebSocket request handling — a client response must be dispatchable while another request is blocked awaiting that dialog.
Idle eviction must not silently drop a pending dialog; either skip eviction or cancel the dialog first.
Pi's dispose() does not emit session_shutdown, so the service must independently clean up UI on eviction/delete/disconnect.
editor() in Pi 0.84.2 has no timeout/signal option; it can only be cancelled by browser response or host/runtime cleanup.
Widget factories cannot be transported over the wire; only string-array form should be bridged.
setEditorText events must be scoped to the active session to avoid overwriting another session's visible draft.
